messages:
AlexH: Quick sync — thinking we should explicitly separate the lease protocol (lease issuance/renewal/invalidation) from admission logic (quota, headroom, fairness) for Dedicated GPU pools. Tradeoffs: simpler operator boundaries vs extra surface for coordination. Thoughts?

MariaG: +1 to separation. Operationally it makes rollouts safer — we can evolve admission heuristics without touching lease semantics. But we need to pin the contract for lease lifecycle (states + invariants).

SamK: Agreed. If we define a small lease contract, operator can be dumb: issue/renew/revoke. Admission/controller takes signals and decides whether to request/hold leases. That also helps in private deployments.

ChenL: Concern: where do we keep accounting for amortized burst credits? If admission logic is outside, someone still needs authoritative bookkeeping for tenant credits to avoid double spends. Do we have a candidate placement?

LinaP: Could use a separate ledger service (eventually optional) that both lease service and admission controllers consult. Or keep soft-state on operator and replicate events to event-sourcing bus. Depends on strong consistency needs.

SamK: For initial version: keep credit ledger inside admission service (single source of truth). Lease protocol should reference tenant id and a lease token, with a flag and TTL. Minimal fields: tenant_id, lease_id, qty, expires_at, strong_consistency_version.

AlexH: Sketch of minimal lease API: 
```
POST /leases         -> {tenant_id, qty} => {lease_id, ttl, ok}
PATCH /leases/:id/renew -> {lease_id} => {ttl}
DELETE /leases/:id   -> revoke
GET /leases?tenant=.. -> list active
```
Important: revoke must be best-effort and support graceful drain semantics.

MariaG: Drain semantics are key — operator must surface connection to runtime to stop scheduling new tasks on draining GPUs. Also need a pre-revoke hook so admission can decide to reduce incoming traffic (eg. score-level throttle).

ChenL: Observability: emit four events for each lifecycle change (issued, renewed, drained, revoked) with tenant+lease metadata. That makes it easy for billing, SLO, and audits. Also add a per-lease cost_estimate field so optimizer can trade cost vs latency.

LinaP: What about emergencies when admission controller becomes unavailable? Do we allow leases to be auto-renewed by operator for a short cooldown to avoid mass failures? We should define failure modes.

SamK: Proposal: leases auto-expire unless renewed. But allow a short grace extension (configurable, e.g., 30s) by operator if admission unresponsive. Also add a quiesce mode where operator rejects new admits but keeps existing leases until TTL.

AlexH: Good. Now policy surface: admission should expose policy primitives not full policy language. Example primitives: Reserve(tenant, qty, duration_hint), ScoreRequest(metrics) -> accept|queue|reject, and HintPrewarm(model_id, prefix_hotness). Keep admission pluggable (we might ship a default controller with heuristics).

MariaG: Can we encode QoS tiers into the lease token? e.g., tier=gold/silver/bronze so operator can map to different scheduler lanes. That reduces coupling later.

ChenL: Yes but be careful — tier implies scheduling latency targets and preemption rules. Make tier optional and validated by admission. Also need to record preemption_policy on lease.

LinaP: Rollout plan idea:
1) Ship lease service behind feature flag in Dedicated control plane (no change to operator behavior).
2) Start routing a small subset of tenants to new admission-controller that uses ledger.
3) Enable revoke/drain hooks and exercise in canary.
4) Gradually flip more traffic and remove the old path.

AlexH: Nice. Action items: 
- SamK: draft lease contract doc + open proto (by EOD Friday)
- ChenL: list required telemetry events and schema (by Monday)
- MariaG: design drain hook API for operator/runtime (by Monday)
- LinaP: propose rollout gating and rollout playbook (by Tuesday)

autoscaler-bot: Note: new RFC PR template created for "lease-admission-split" — link: https://git/repo/pulls/2412 :robot_face:

SamK: I'll start the proto and include example flows (admit success, backpressure, preempt). Will ping infra for GC semantics.

MariaG: If anyone has objections to the separation approach speak up now; otherwise I'll write up a short follow-up RFC section about operator vs controller responsibilities.

ChenL: No objections from me. Also: add a metric for lease-staleness and ledger-conflicts.

LinaP: OK from me. Thanks all.

AlexH: Great sync — will follow up on the RFC and link the PR in this thread. :thumbsup:
